mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur when UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts and retail sales signal strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow when both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth during late-cycle expansion signals continued economic strength, leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not occur during late-cycle with INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow increasing PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 2000 signals weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur when HOUST falls below 2000.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with low GDP signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow when FEDFUNDS is high and GDPC1 is low.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate during tightening cycles may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur during tightening with FEDFUNDS increase.
